analysis.title: Systematic Flows Monitor: CTAs start covering long-end UST shorts as tech selloff kicks off equity unwinds
key_insights: CTAs have begun covering stretched US Treasury futures shorts at the long end, with unwinds underway in UXY, US and WN contracts. They remain short TU, FV and TY, so covering risk is substantial if the rally extends.

TU and TY futures ended Friday just off BofA's first CTA buy-trigger levels. Industry positioning may be about $280bn in 10yr equivalents, implying roughly $170mn of buying per basis point during an unwind.
Equity weakness and the first CTA short reductions likely reinforced a global bull-flattening move in rates. Covering is also underway at the back end of the European curve.
CTA equity exposure is still long overall, but breadth is deteriorating. Nasdaq-100 and Nikkei longs have begun to stop out after the tech selloff, and more selling is possible next week.
Faster-moving CTA models are building Russell 2000 shorts. Weakening Euro Stoxx 50 trends leave that positioning vulnerable to further unwinds.

S&P 500 CTA longs remain intact, but the nearest sell trigger is only 1.1% away (long unwind could begin at 7,624 versus 7,696 current). Higher realized volatility should also reduce CTA position sizes in equity markets where they are long.

Systematic strategies (CTAs, risk parity, vol control) could sell $81bn of global equities in a down market, $10bn if flat and $3bn in an up market. Selling in the down case would be led by CTAs and vol control, and by the US by region.

Trend followers remain broadly long USD despite this week's dollar weakness. EUR and CAD shorts are the most stretched positions. Projections point to USD buying next week against AUD and MXN, while falling USDCAD brings the risk of USD selling as CAD buy triggers move closer.

CTAs are stretched long crude after WTI moved above $100. Flow risk is increasingly negative elsewhere in commodities: gold and aluminum trends are firmly bearish, weaker copper momentum could bring more metals selling, and soybean and soybean oil longs have begun to stop out.

SPX delta-hedger gamma ended 15-Oct at $15.2bn (99th percentile in the last year), the second straight week above the 90th percentile at every close. The 16-Oct monthly expiry contributed $7.0bn, while 1DTE selling flow was lighter than the prior week.

SPX 5-day intraday realized volatility rose only modestly to 11% (33rd percentile) despite the SPX selloff, NDX underperformance and VIX briefly trading above 20 on 16-Oct. High dealer gamma is the suppressing factor.

Delta-hedgers averaged net long $16.6bn of SPX gamma intraday over 5 days: +$10.1bn non-expiring, +$2.6bn 0DTE and +$3.9bn expiring open interest. If hedging were confined to the last 15 minutes, gamma would have cut e-mini 1-month realized vol by about 1.3 points (12%).

US leveraged and inverse ETFs need to trade about $1.1bn (S&P 500) and $2.6bn (Nasdaq-100) per 1% index move, both lower than last week. That is about 3% and 22% of average notional traded from 3:55 to 4:00 PM.

Single-stock leveraged ETFs are led by NVDA ($4.3bn AUM) and TSLA ($4.0bn), with rebalance needs of about $95mn and $94mn per 1% move. NVDA, TSLA, MU and SNDK leveraged ETF AUM each fell over $500mn on the week.

Total CTA assets are $425.5bn per BarclayHedge as of 2026-Q1. BofA's model assumes $300bn in CTAs and $200bn each in risk parity and vol control, and systematic global equity positioning is above its five-year median.

macro_indicators.interpretation: CTAs remain stretched long crude after WTI moved above $100, which leaves the trade exposed to a reversal.
VIX spiked during the tech selloff while SPX realized vol stayed low at 11%.

risk_factors: Further tech weakness could trigger more Nasdaq-100 and Nikkei CTA long unwinds and S&P 500 longs if the 7,624 sell trigger is hit.
A continued Treasury rally would force more CTA short covering in TU, FV and TY.
Rising realized volatility would shrink CTA and vol-control equity position sizes.
Stretched CTA long crude and short EUR and CAD positions are vulnerable to reversals.
Different CTA implementations trade at different levels, so model triggers are hard to pin down.
BofA's leveraged ETF estimate cannot account for same-day creations and redemptions.

vol_and_positioning: SPX hedger gamma ended 15-Oct at $15.2bn, 99th percentile in the last year, and above the 90th percentile at every close for two straight weeks.
SPX 5-day intraday realized volatility ticked up to 11% (33rd percentile) while VIX briefly traded above 20 on 16-Oct.
Of 15-Oct gamma, the 16-Oct monthly expiry accounted for $7.0bn. 1DTE selling was lighter than the prior week.
CTAs are short TU, FV and TY and covering UXY, US and WN. Industry short may be about $280bn in 10yr equivalents.
CTA equity longs are narrowing: Nasdaq-100 and Nikkei stopping out, Russell 2000 shorts being built, Euro Stoxx 50 trends weakening, S&P 500 sell trigger 1.1% away.
CTAs remain broadly long USD, with EUR and CAD shorts most stretched, and long crude.
Gold and aluminum CTA trends are firmly bearish. Soybean and soybean oil longs have begun to stop out.
Leveraged and inverse ETF rebalancing is about $1.1bn per 1% SPX move and $2.6bn per 1% NDX move.
